title: Structured admin audit federation and sealed batch exports
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Admin actions, permission changes, and configuration edits are currently captured in the event store, but there is no standardized, residency-aware sealed export path for long-term immutable evidence. Compliance teams require chain-of-custody artifacts for audits, plus a way to produce residency-scoped WORM bundles for retention and legal hold. This ticket designs a federated audit pipeline that provides both low-latency append-only telemetry for product queries and periodic sealed exports for tamper-evident archival storage.
background: Current audit capture: eventbus -> eventstore (mutable backing), with ad-hoc snapshot exports. Existing work on tamper evidence covers single-region anchoring but lacks: (1) per-customer residency enforcement, (2) standardized signed manifests for bundle verification, and (3) an automated export automation with retention tagging and legal-hold override flows.
proposed_design: Two-path architecture: 1) Real-time path: produce structured audit records to a dedicated append-only topic and materialize into queryable index with enforced write-only ACLs and immutability markers. 2) Sealed export path: weekly and monthly batch exporters create residency-scoped bundles into S3 buckets with Object Lock (Compliance mode). Each bundle contains normalized NDJSON, a signed manifest including Merkle root, per-record sequence numbers, and state digests. Signing is performed by an HSM-backed KMS key; manifests are also timestamped by an external RFC-3161 timestamping service. Bundles are stored in geo-separated buckets per residency and replicated to an escrow bucket for long-term preservation. A verification endpoint will compute Merkle roots from downloaded bundles and verify KMS signatures and timestamp stamps.
scope: In-scope: event normalization schema, append-only topic schema, sealed exporter job, manifest format, KMS/HSM signing integration, S3 Object Lock configuration, residency tagging/enforcement, verification CLI and API. Out-of-scope: UI for audit browsing (follow-up), archival search UX, marketplace billing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Structured audit records emitted for admin actions (create/delete/modify role, login/impersonation, config changes) with stable schema v1
Append-only topic configured with write-only producer credentials and immutability markers; records immutable for 30 days in stream
Sealed exporter produces residency-scoped bundles stored with S3 Object Lock (Compliance); each bundle includes a signed manifest (KMS) and RFC-3161 timestamp
Verification API accepts a bundle and returns pass/fail for signature and Merkle root checks
Retention tags applied per-customer policy and legal-hold overrides respected by exporter automation
Automated smoke tests and end-to-end verification run in CI; regression tests for manifest format included
Security review completed and KMS key policy audited
Documentation: runbook for generating ad-hoc sealed exports for auditors and steps for verifying integrity locally
implementation_plan: Design normalization schema and sample payloads with PM/Compliance
Add append-only topic and update producers to write structured records
Implement exporter worker: read windowed events, normalize, compute Merkle tree, generate manifest, call KMS sign, request RFC-3161 timestamp, upload bundle to residency bucket with Object Lock
Create verification service/CLI to validate manifest signature and Merkle proof
Add retention tags and legal-hold checks to exporter; wire to policy service
End-to-end QA: run in staging with synthetic cross-region datasets
Security review and key policy hardening, then cut release to runtime-2.3
rollout_plan: Stage 0: feature flag gated in staging; exporter writes to staging buckets only
Stage 1: Canary export for internal org using non-production keys and separate residency buckets
Stage 2: Opt-in export for pilot customers (compliance customers) with manual verification
Stage 3: Gradual enablement for customers with retention defaults; monitor costs and throughput
Stage 4: Full GA after 2 weeks of stable pilot and signoff from Legal and Security
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for normalization and manifest generation
Property tests for Merkle tree generation and deterministic roots
Integration tests for KMS signing and RFC-3161 timestamping (mocked in CI, real in staging)
E2E tests that upload a bundle to a test bucket and validate verification CLI
Load test exporter to ensure export windows complete within SLA for large customers
Failure mode tests: partial upload, interrupted worker, key rotation scenarios
monitoring_and_alerting: Exporter job success/failure rate and latency SLOs
Bundle integrity check alerts on verification failures
KMS signing error rate and HSM availability metrics
Cost anomaly alert for export egress or large bundle sizes
operational_runbook: How to generate ad-hoc sealed export for an auditor: CLI steps, required IAM roles, verification steps
Key rotation playbook: how to re-sign manifests for historical bundles and annotate manifests
Legal hold procedure: freeze exporter deletion for specified customer tag
Recovery: rebuilding a bundle from append-only topic if upload corrupted
notes: Considerations for on-prem/private deployments: allow configuring local object-store and KMS endpoint; ensure manifests include exporter version and local key fingerprints
S3 Object Lock is used in Compliance mode to meet WORM, but legal hold must be surfaced to UI/console (PM follow-up)
We recommend a 2-year default retention for admin audit bundles but make retention configurable per customer and per residency
External notarization increases trust for auditors; evaluate cost vs. benefit with Legal
Edge case: short-lived ephemeral keys for exporters need careful sequencing to avoid unverifiable bundles
